headline: Fire at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital: Reports of 6 stampede deaths denied by administration
summary: Panic erupted at MMCH after a fire broke out in the new building, leading to reports of multiple deaths from a stampede, which officials have since disputed.
details: A fire broke out in the new building of Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH) on Monday afternoon, triggering widespread panic among patients and their relatives.
The fire reportedly started around 5:30 PM due to an electrical short circuit in the lift control room on the eighth floor.
As thick black smoke filled the corridors and wards, people rushed to evacuate the building through narrow staircases, leading to chaos.
Initial reports suggested that at least six people, including a child, were killed in a stampede during the evacuation process.
However, the divisional commissioner and hospital administration have denied these reports, stating that the information regarding deaths is being verified and is incorrect.
Four units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence arrived promptly at the scene and managed to bring the fire under control.
Several people were injured during the panic and were treated in the hospital's emergency department.
Law enforcement agencies have been working to identify those affected as the administration investigates the cause of the incident.
caption:
Panic at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital after a fire triggers a chaotic evacuation. Reports of 6 deaths are being disputed by officials.

A fire broke out in the new building of Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH) on Monday afternoon, triggering widespread panic among patients and their relatives.

The fire reportedly started around 5:30 PM due to an electrical short circuit in the lift control room on the eighth floor.

As thick black smoke filled the corridors and wards, people rushed to evacuate the building through narrow staircases, leading to chaos.

Initial reports suggested that at least six people, including a child, were killed in a stampede during the evacuation process.

However, the divisional commissioner and hospital administration have denied these reports, stating that the information regarding deaths is being verified and is incorrect.

Four units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence arrived promptly at the scene and managed to bring the fire under control.

Several people were injured during the panic and were treated in the hospital's emergency department.

Law enforcement agencies have been working to identify those affected as the administration investigates the cause of the incident.

Source: Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star

headline: Student group backlash over Jinnah photos in Ducsu archive
summary: Jatiya Chhatra Shakti criticizes the display of Muhammad Ali Jinnah's photo, alleging an attempt to make Pakistan-leaning politics relevant again.
details: The Jatiya Chhatra Shakti student organization has criticized the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (Ducsu) for displaying a photograph of Muhammad Ali Jinnah and presenting him 'heroically' in its archive.
caption:
Is Pakistan-leaning politics being revived at Dhaka University? A student group is sounding the alarm over photos in the Ducsu archive.

The Jatiya Chhatra Shakti student organization has criticized the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (Ducsu) for displaying a photograph of Muhammad Ali Jinnah and presenting him 'heroically' in its archive.
